Schematic of proposed SDF modules, both hardware and software • SDF is most impactful when it is able to provide quantitative information on encountered radiation sources, i.e., source strengths, as well as their spatial distributions in environments with clutter and shielding. This will require the fusion of multiple datastreams, each of which conveys partial information. This will be challenging, as the complexity grows in a combinatorial fashion with the number of sensing modalities being available for fusion. • Many quantitative source estimation algorithms should be integrated with model selection methods in order to determine the type of source being estimated by SDF. The nature/type of the source is as important as the quantitative estimate. • Both users and autonomous algorithms may benefit from ‘meta-algorithms’ to help guide model selection, optimize imaging algorithm parameters, and monitor whether sufficient data has been collected. • Most applications have not been subjected to a dedicated study of mission-specific SDF equipment development, algorithm development, user interface implementation, and CONOP development/adjustment. • The computers carried by SDF-capable systems are often tasked at 100% during data acquisition and online data processing. Improvements in computational efficiency, enabling data offloading to better (cloud-based) compute resources, and/or implementation of computational trade-offs could all improve SDF system performance for most applications. These common themes behind SDF enhancements lead us to propose some research thrust areas for SDF, as described below. LBNL Report #2001653 5.1 Modular Development Platform SDF can be thought of as containing four different layers: a mobile platform; sensors and instrumentation; software capabilities that help overlay and visualize the reconstructions of the source (or the surrounding context) obtained via individual sensing modalities; and finally the quantitative estimation of the source (and/or identification of the surrounding context) by fusing the data-streams.
